title: AI-discovered proof resolves the Komlós vector-balancing conjecture
summary: The paper proves that for every finite family of Euclidean-norm-at-most-one vectors, signs can be chosen so the signed sum has infinity norm below 3√(2π), independent of vector count and dimension. It derives a corresponding square-root-in-sets bound for Beck–Fiala discrepancy. The authors explicitly credit the Odin Automatic AI Research Agent with discovering the proof; a separate elementary proof was posted independently. The algorithmic construction of such signings is a separate follow-up result and is not claimed here.
organization: Duke University; University of California, Irvine; independent research collaboration

evidence.tested: The paper proves that for every finite family of Euclidean-norm-at-most-one vectors, signs can be chosen so the signed sum has infinity norm below 3√(2π), independent of vector count and dimension.
evidence.unknown: The result is reported in an arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal source in this review. A separate elementary proof of the conjecture appeared later, providing an independent proof route; the paper’s AI attribution is author-reported. The result establishes existence, not a polynomial-time signing algorithm.
evidence.ai_role: The authors credit Odin with discovering the proof of their vector-balancing theorem; Duke’s official account says the system discovered the proof and human authors scrutinized and organized the argument into the paper.
